investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-19T18:36–18:43Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible to run peer-pod workloads. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector, and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~137–147 seconds before the eval timed out, and no VM identity or state was ever returned to the runner. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed between 18:38 and 18:43 UTC on 2026-07-19 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity had none remaining, and the other 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the eval produced zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every remote agent pod submitted by the eval runner is stuck Unschedulable, preventing agent creation and causing all downstream checks (state, runtime) to fail with empty evidence. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes carry, and those 2 nodes are also the only ones with kata.peerpods.io/vm. If the affinity is overly restrictive, even partial VM availability on other nodes would not help.

Tertiary — a concurrent workload spike or leaked/zombie remote agent pods from prior eval runs consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, leaving no capacity for new scheduling attempts.

Lower probability — a cluster node failure or cordon that reduced the effective kata.peerpods.io/vm pool below the minimum needed to schedule eval pods, combined with the affinity constraint preventing fallback to other nodes.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-19T18:36–18:43Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible to run peer-pod workloads. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector, and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~137–147 seconds before the eval timed out, and no VM identity or state was ever returned to the runner. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed between 18:38 and 18:43 UTC on 2026-07-19 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity had none remaining, and the other 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the eval produced zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every remote agent pod submitted by the eval runner is stuck Unschedulable, preventing agent creation and causing all downstream checks (state, runtime) to fail with empty evidence. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes carry, and those 2 nodes are also the only ones with kata.peerpods.io/vm. If the affinity is overly restrictive, even partial VM availability on other nodes would not help.

Tertiary — a concurrent workload spike or leaked/zombie remote agent pods from prior eval runs consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, leaving no capacity for new scheduling attempts.

Lower probability — a cluster node failure or cordon that reduced the effective kata.peerpods.io/vm pool below the minimum needed to schedule eval pods, combined with the affinity constraint preventing fallback to other nodes.
